articles.headline: 2026 NFL awards tracker: Odds for MVP, Rookie of the Year and more
articles.description: Who are the favorites to win seasonlong honors? Here are the odds for MVP, Rookie of the Year and more.
articles.headlineJa: 2026年NFLアワード追跡：MVP、新人王などのオッズ
articles.descriptionJa: シーズン最優秀賞を勝ち取る本命は誰か？MVPや新人王などの最新オッズを紹介します。
articles.body:
A quarter of the way through the season, there are two clear MVP frontrunners, according to the odds. Josh Allen, the favorite coming into the season at +600, has shortened to +250 after another dazzling performance on "Monday Night Football," but Brock Purdy continues to challenge him at +300 and was briefly the favorite coming out of Sunday's slate. Purdy came into the campaign with 10th-best 18-1 odds.

Patrick Mahomes is the third favorite for MVP at +650, as well as the odds-on favorite for Comeback Player of the Year at -300. Drake Maye has recovered nicely after a horrible start to the season that saw his MVP odds go to a long of 80-1, making it back to 17-1.

Jahmyr Gibbs has retaken control of the Offensive Player of the Year race as the +280 favorite, with Bijan Robinson and Kenneth Walker III -- who was on bye in Week 5 -- trailing just behind at +400. On the other side of the ball, Will Anderson Jr. has become the clear favorite for Defensive Player of the Year at +125, improving from his second-best +500 at the beginning of the season.

Offensive Rookie of the Year has also seen some significant movement, with Denzel Boston (+175) taking away favorite status from Jeremiyah Love (+225), while Carnell Tate is staying within striking distance at +500.

Odds by DraftKings.  Super Bowl odds can be found here.

articles.headline: Super Bowl LXI odds: All 32 teams' odds to win the championship
articles.description: Every NFL team's win total, as well as odds to win the division, the conference and Super Bowl LXI.
articles.headlineJa: スーパーボウル LXI オッズ：全32チームの優勝確率
articles.descriptionJa: 全NFLチームの勝利数予想に加え、地区優勝、カンファレンス優勝、そしてスーパーボウル LXI制覇のオッズを掲載。
articles.body:
After beginning the season as the clear Super Bowl favorites at +500, the Los Angeles Rams' grip on the top spot has loosened significantly. After a 2-3 start, they are now tied with the division rival San Francisco 49ers at +700 to win Super Bowl LXI. L.A.'s latest loss came via an overtime thriller Monday night to the Buffalo Bills, who are tied for the second-best odds on the board with the Baltimore Ravens at +800.

The next tier consists of the Kansas City Chiefs, who lengthened slightly from +900 to +950 during their bye week, and the Seattle Seahawks, who fell from +950 to 11-1 week-over-week after their close loss to San Francisco.

The Jacksonville Jaguars continue to gain ground after beginning the season at 30-1, making it all the way to 12-1. The undefeated Minnesota Vikings have also been a notable improver, tied with three other teams at 20-1 after coming into the campaign at 50-1.

The season's biggest disappointment is undoubtedly the Los Angeles Chargers, who began the season with sixth-best 17-1 odds and have fallen virtually out of contention to 200-1 after an 0-5 start.

Note: Odds by DraftKings  and subject to change.

articles.headline: Unai Emery keen for Aston Villa to use home advantage in Fenerbahce clash
articles.description: Aston Villa boss Unai Emery wants his side to enjoy their home comforts once again when they host Fenerbahce in the Champions League.
articles.headlineJa: ウナイ・エメリ監督、フェネルバフチェ戦でアストン・ヴィラのホームアドバンテージ活用に意欲
articles.descriptionJa: アストン・ヴィラのウナイ・エメリ監督は、チャンピオンズリーグでフェネルバフチェをホームに迎える際、再びホームの利を最大限に活かしたいと考えている。
articles.body:
Aston Villa boss Unai Emery wants his side to enjoy their home comforts once again when they host Fenerbahce in the Champions League.

The side's form at Villa Park has been one of the driving forces behind Villa's rise to the top of the English game, where they are once again competing in the European Cup for the second time in three years.

But they are enduring a tough time of it on home soil this season, having lost two and drawn the other of their opening three games.

That may be in part due to the fact they are only playing in front of three sides this season as the North Stand gets refurbished in time for Euro 2028, with the building site affecting the atmosphere.

But Emery thinks it is time to put it right against the Turkish outfit on Wednesday night.

- Unai Emery 'sad' after Aston Villa draw with Brentford

- How Aston Villa boss Unai Emery rescued Real Unión, his 'family' club, from ruin

"We are realistic about how we are working and improving things," he said at a news conference on Tuesday. "But it is not enough yet, so we are having lots of conversations with the team, in meetings and with videos, practicing too to show improvements in matches.

"At Villa Park, we have not won yet, so it is very important how we can improve things to be closer to winning. Tomorrow is a very good opportunity to do one step forward in those improvements and the players as well to get confidence and feel comfortable.

"Villa Park is for us something very, very special. It should be like the four years that we are here -- how we achieved this as a special place, our fortress. Tomorrow is a new challenge to show it."

Villa's inconsistent start to the season has not been helped by injuries and they have suffered another blow in the build-up to the second round of Champions League fixtures.

Matteo Ruggeri came off at half-time of Saturday's 2-2 draw with Brentford, leaving a gap at left-back with Ian Maatsen still out.

George Hemmings will miss out but Leon Goretzka could be set for a debut as he builds his fitness up following a knee injury which has curtailed the first few weeks of his Villa Park stay.

Brian Madjo and Taylor Harwood-Bellis are ineligible having been left out of the Champions League squad.

"There are negative ways for some players, because they are injured like Ruggeri," Emery said.

"We must try to find solutions as Maatsen is not available. I think he should be in a few days, one week or two weeks joining us.

"Ruggeri, we don't know exactly how long it's going to be, but it will be some weeks that he's going to be out, more than one month. We need to find solutions because [Ian] Maatsen is not yet available.

"I think, the way he is, getting better, he should be joining us in a few days or a week, so it's positive.

"Leon Goretzka is in the squad for tomorrow; George Hemmings is still being with a small pain -- not [available] for tomorrow but maybe on Saturday he can come back

articles.headline: Sources: 76ers' G League affiliate in Delaware tabs Brad Jones as GM
articles.description: The Delaware Blue Coats, the 76ers' G League affiliate, are hiring Brad Jones as their next general manager, team sources told ESPN.
articles.headlineJa: 【情報】76ers傘下のGリーグ・デラウェアチームがブラッド・ジョーンズ氏をGMに任命
articles.descriptionJa: チーム関係者がESPNに語ったところによると、76ersのGリーグ傘下チームであるデラウェア・ブルーコーツは、次期ゼネラルマネージャーとしてブラッド・ジョーンズ氏を起用する。
articles.body:
The Delaware Blue Coats, the Philadelphia 76ers' G League affiliate, are hiring Brad Jones as their next general manager, team sources told ESPN.

Jones was selected, sources said, by Sixers president Mike Gansey and executive vice president of basketball operations Jameer Nelson, after former Blue Coats GM Ariana Andonian left to run the WNBA's Los Angeles Sparks last month.

Jones began his career with the Orlando Magic when Nelson played there, working his way up from being an intern to serving on the video and personnel staff.

He most recently has worked in the G League offices in New York for the past eight years and was involved in player contracts and transactions, basketball operations and basketball affairs and player personnel.

Delaware went 18-18 last season. The Blue Coats will open the 2026-27 G League season on Nov. 6 at home against the Capital City Go-Go.

articles.headline: 2026 NFL pass rush, run stop, blocking win rate rankings
articles.description: Our win rate metrics stack the NFL's top teams and players in run blocking, run stopping, pass protection and pass rushing.
articles.headlineJa: 2026年NFLパスラッシュ、ランストップ、ブロッキング勝率ランキング
articles.descriptionJa: 当サイトの勝率指標に基づき、ランブロッキング、ランストップ、パスプロテクション、パスラッシュにおけるNFLのトップチームと選手をランク付けします。
articles.body:
ESPN Analytics created revolutionary metrics to measure performance in the trenches -- in both the run and pass game -- using player tracking data from NFL Next Gen Stats. And we updated the formula a little bit for 2026 -- see what's new here.

Our pass rush win rate metric tells us how often a pass rusher is able to beat/win his block within 2.5 seconds. Likewise, our pass block win rate metric conveys the rate linemen can sustain their blocks for 2.5 seconds or longer.

In run stop win rate, a defender can earn a win by doing any of the following: beating his blocker so he's in better position to stop the runner; disrupting the pocket or running lane by pushing his blocker backward; containing the runner such that he must adjust his running lane; or recording a tackle within 3 yards of the line of scrimmage. If a defender earns a run stop win, his blocker earns a loss -- and vice versa.

Here are the rankings for each metric for the 2026 NFL season.

articles.headline: Clarence Seedorf: I understand why Kobbie Mainoo is compared to me
articles.description: AC Milan and Ajax legend Clarence Seedorf told Manchester United midfielder Kobbie Mainoo that he sees similarities between himself and the England international.
articles.headlineJa: クラレンス・セードルフ：「コビー・メイヌーが自分と比較される理由はわかる」
articles.descriptionJa: ACミランとアヤックスのレジェンドであるクラレンス・セードルフが、マンチェスター・ユナイテッドのMFコビー・メイヌーに対し、自分とこのイングランド代表選手に共通点があると感じると語りました。
articles.body:
AC Milan and Ajax legend Clarence Seedorf told Manchester United midfielder Kobbie Mainoo that he sees similarities between himself and the England international.

Seedorf paid a visit to United's Carrington training complex to interview Mainoo for Amazon Prime Video Sport and addressed the fact that Mainoo is often referred to by fans as the "Stockport Seedorf."

"People compare us sometimes, maybe too much. I didn't like to be compared when I was young. I think everybody's unique. I think you're a unique player," the Dutchman told Mainoo.

"I think you have a similar mindset as I had at a young age. The way you read the match and the way you are calm, which is a great attribute to have because when pressure comes for the team, they can rely on you."

Seedorf and Mainoo discussed Champions League matches and the special feeling that the tournament has. Seedorf remains the only player to ever win Europe's biggest club competition with three different clubs.

"It feels like it's so long ago. Well, I know it's only a few years, but it feels like so long ago just because it feels like a lot has happened. A lot of matches and a lot has happened," Mainoo said when asked about his Champions League debut in 2023.

"To be where we are now, you know, obviously we could be doing better in the league, which we will, we will get better. But to be qualified for Champions League and hearing that music and walking out at Old Trafford, you know, is special.

"My first season was my first glimpse of Champions League football and I was young, 18, and I'd come on against Bayern Munich and Galatasaray and I came in the late stages and we were out, so I was like, "Oh, I need to feel that again," you know?

"I need to be under those lights again and to be back there. So it's amazing."

Seedorf spoke about winning the Champions League with his idol Frank Rijkaard and being driven when he was a young player to win as many Champions League titles as Rijkaard did.

He asked Mainoo what his drive is at United and the midfielder said he wants to bring the glory days back to Old Trafford.

"Obviously with a boss like Michael Carrick, who's won here, and he knows about the golden times with Man United, I want to bring that back, you know?" Mainoo told Seedorf.

"I want to feel that. Everyone talks about Manchester United in the past, you know, and I want to bring that to now, and I want to win. I want to win a lot here, you know? That's my dream, for this club to be at the top again."

In response, Seedorf said: "It's beautiful that you talk about your coach.

- Man United could never contend for the Premier League title -- but they aren't so bad either

- Carrick backs Man United for UCL rebound amid challenging spell

- Premier League overreactions: Takeaways from first games post-international break

"Michael has been a great professional, a great player. He will be a great manager as well. He's done good things I've seen from the outside. He brought you back in the pitch

articles.headline: Liverpool's Alexander Isak, Cody Gakpo, Dominik Szoboszlai to miss Champions League clash with LASK
articles.description: Liverpool are set to be without Alexander Isak, Cody Gakpo and Dominik Szoboszlai for Wednesday's UEFA Champions League clash with LASK.
articles.headlineJa: リヴァプールのイサク、ガクポ、ソボスライがLASKとのチャンピオンズリーグ戦を欠場へ
articles.descriptionJa: リヴァプールは、水曜日に開催されるUEFAチャンピオンズリーグのLASK戦に、アレクサンダー・イサク、コディ・ガクポ、ドミニク・ソボスライの3名を欠場させる見通しです。
articles.body:
Liverpool are set to be without Alexander Isak, Cody Gakpo and Dominik Szoboszlai for Wednesday's UEFA Champions League clash with LASK.

All three players missed the Reds' 3-0 defeat to Manchester City on Sunday after sustaining injuries during the international break. Isak and Gakpo both had to withdraw from international duty with a thigh injury and an ankle injury respectively while Szoboszlai returned from the Hungary camp with a tight hamstring.

The trio have all failed to recover in time for Wednesday's clash at Raiffeisen Arena and are not part of Liverpool's 23-player travelling party to Austria.

Speaking about Szoboszlai's fitness at the weekend, Iraola said: "Dom came from the national team with tightness, an overload. We put him as a floater in the training and tried to protect him but he was feeling something very small. It's true that now we play four games in 10 days, so it's going to be difficult because we fly to Austria in two days. I think it's going to be difficult to recover any of the players."

The Liverpool boss is expected to give a further update on the players' fitness in his prematch news conference on Tuesday.

articles.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Barcelona, Real Madrid scout Erling Haaland at Anfield
articles.description: Barcelona and Real Madrid continue to keep tabs on Erling Haaland, while Chelsea growing confident of signing Bournemouth's Alex Scott. Transfer Talk has the latest.
articles.headlineJa: 移籍の噂とニュース：バルセロナとレアル・マドリードがアンフィールドでアーリング・ハーランドを視察
articles.descriptionJa: バルセロナとレアル・マドリードが引き続きアーリング・ハーランドをマークする一方、チェルシーはボーンマスのアレックス・スコット獲得に自信を深めています。「トランスファー・トーク」が最新情報を伝えます。
articles.body:
Barcelona and Real Madrid were at Anfield on Sunday to watch Erling Haaland when Manchester City faced Liverpool. Meanwhile, Chelsea are growing confident they will be able to sign AFC Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott in January.

Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Barcelona and Real Madrid scouts were at Anfield to scout Manchester City striker Erling Haaland as he opened the scoring in a 3-0 win over Liverpool, according to TEAMtalk. Both of the Spanish giants continue to monitor the possibility of a future move following the club's guilty verdict for hundreds of financial charges. The two clubs weren't just there to watch City players, though: Barça have also been monitoring the situation of defender Ronald Araújo, who is on loan at Liverpool, while Madrid have been checking on Liverpool midfielders Alexis Mac Allister and Florian Wirtz.

- Chelsea are increasingly confident that they will sign AFC Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott during the January transfer window, according to TEAMtalk. The belief is that the 23-year-old would find it difficult to turn down a move to Stamford Bridge and the Blues are willing to meet the Cherries' demands, with any deal likely to reach around £100 million. Bournemouth turned down all interest in Scott during the summer, but the England international's contract expires in 2028 and he has so far resisted any calls for an extension.

- Borussia Dortmund have been interested in U.S. youth international and Philadelphia Union striker Malik Jakupovic for some time, reports Sky Germany. In the summer, the Bundesliga club submitted an offer for the 17-year-old that was worth €2m-€3m but was ultimately rejected. Contact continues to exist but there is major competition for Jakupovic with Chelsea, RB Salzburg and Stuttgart all looking at him while Eintracht Frankfurt also have in the past.

- Chelsea will need at least £50 million to tempt Barcelona into letting midfielder Frenkie de Jong leave in the January transfer window, according to Football Insider. Chelsea are looking at the 29-year-old as they continue their efforts to replace Enzo Fernández after the Argentina international joined Manchester City in the summer. De Jong is out injured but the Dutch midfield is nearing a return to fitness, although that return could make a move more difficult for the Blues as Barça have been eagerly awaiting his return.

- Ruben Amorim wants AC Milan to sign Sassuolo midfielder Darryl Bakola, who has also received interest from Roma and Juventus, reports Calciomercato. Amorim was surprised by the 18-year-old's quality when the Rossoneri drew 1-1 against Sassuolo at Mapei Stadium, when Bakola was named man of the match. The young Frenchman is being considered by scouts across Europe, and having been signed for €10 million plus €2 million in add-ons last January, he could now command over €30 million.

articles.headline: Which NBA deals will get done? Bobby Marks' biggest extension decisions to watch
articles.description: With Monday's extension deadline looming, Bobby Marks breaks down the biggest decisions around the league.
articles.headlineJa: NBAのどの契約が成立するか？ボビー・マークスが注目する主要な延長契約の決定事項
articles.descriptionJa: 月曜日の延長契約期限が迫る中、ボビー・マークスがリーグ全体における最大の注目決定事項について解説します。
articles.body:
The NBA season starts in one week, but that isn't the only thing on the minds of league executives. The deadline for rookie extensions is Monday, a day before the 2026-27 regular season tips off. 

Since the start of the offseason, five players -- Victor Wembanyama, Amen and Ausar Thompson, Keyonte George and Brandin Podziemski -- have signed rookie extensions. That's currently far below the average of 11 rookie extensions signed per year since 2023, but expect that number to rise in the coming days. Of the 34 players to land rookie extensions in the past three seasons, 17 signed on deadline day.

What deals will the next week bring? We broke down what to expect for six of the 16 eligible players.

Rookie extension decisions aren't the only things we're watching. Oct. 19 is also the deadline to extend veterans with two years remaining on their contract -- not including an option year -- and the deadline to reduce rosters to 15 players on standard contracts.

Let's examine the league's most important extension decisions and what Monday's deadline could bring for teams around the league.

Jump to a section:

Six big rookie extension decisions

KAT, Giannis among vets to watch

Moves coming for Lakers, Knicks?

Rookie extension candidates to watch

Brandon Miller, Charlotte Hornets

Why an extension could get done: Following offseason trades of LaMelo Ball and Miles Bridges, the Hornets view Miller and Kon Knueppel as the franchise's new foundation. An injury-plagued sophomore 2024-25 season limited Miller to 27 games, but he rebounded last season to post career highs in 3-pointers made, 3-point percentage and free throw attempts and averaged more than 20 points per game for the second straight season.

 

Why it might not: Miller views Amen Thompson's five-year, $208 million extension with Houston as a comparable salary. The main difference: Thompson played at least 60 games in each of his first three seasons and was selected for the All-Defensive First Team in 2025.

What I would offer: Five years, $175 million. The contract can either start at $30.2 million and increase each year, ending at $39.8 million, or start high and decline each season. (Coby White's latest contract with the Hornets declines in Years 2 and 3.) With no player earning more than $25 million in 2027-28, Charlotte has the flexibility to increase Miller's offer. Not including new contracts for Miller and center Moussa Diabate, who is eligible for an extension in February, Charlotte projects to be $80 million under the luxury tax next season.

Dereck Lively II, Dallas Mavericks

Why an extension could get done: The Mavericks would need to bypass injury concerns and look at his impact when healthy. Despite playing only 36 games in 2024-25, Lively ranked 17th out of 138 players in offensive rebounding percentage and fourth in defensive rebounding percentage.
